Plainly: A BEL will hold, with A PIC supporting. I won’t give Belgium back while it is my center; F NTH–BEL will bounce. Please keep F NTH out of BEL and the Channel, and let’s avoid turning this into a wider conflict.
I’ll leave MAR unchallenged and keep A SPA and F GAS clear of your centers. F GAS will help protect Spain; please keep A PIE out of GAS and SPA and don’t move F GOL against Spain.
Yes. A RUH will attack MUN; please support it with A BOH. I’ll keep my other units out of Austrian centers. If we recover MUN from Russia, let’s keep the frontier stable afterward.

I can’t leave F DEN occupying my center unchallenged. F HEL will attack DEN, with A HOL supporting. I won’t attack HOL or HEL, but I can’t promise to keep F HEL away from DEN while your fleet remains there.

Yes: F GOL–MAR, supported by A PIE. I’ll keep A PIE out of GAS and SPA and won’t advance beyond MAR this turn. Please keep A SPA and F GAS from contesting MAR as you proposed, so we can contain the dispute.

I’m maintaining neutrality in the Balkan contest this fall. F ADR will stay clear of GRE and the Ionian, and I ask you to keep your forces clear of Italian centers as agreed. We can revisit coordination next spring if Austria threatens my position.

A MUN will hold, with A SIL supporting it. I will keep A SIL out of HOL and KIE this fall, but I can’t vacate MUN while it is a supply center I can secure. I’m willing to keep the remaining German centers clear and discuss a stable boundary afterward.

A MUN will hold with A SIL supporting; I have no A BER. I’ll keep my moves clear of French centers. Your pressure on HOL complements my position against Germany—please let me know if A BEL–HOL with A PIC support is still your plan.

A MUN will hold with A SIL supporting; I’m focused on Germany and will keep A SIL out of BOH and your centers. F RUM will stay clear of the Balkans. To give F GRE its best chance, A SER can support it to hold; I can’t support Greece from RUM.
A MUN will hold with A SIL supporting; I have no A BER. F SKA will move to SWE, not DEN or NOR, and I’ll keep F BOT clear of Denmark. I’m glad you’re leaving SWE and NOR alone.

Yes. F RUM will stay clear of the Balkans, and A ARM will stay clear of your centers. I won’t support Austria against your move this fall. Please continue keeping your forces out of RUM and the Black Sea.

A BUL will attack GRE, supported by A CON and F AEG; I will keep A SER and your other centers clear. I understand you are considering pressure on BUL, but an attack there would widen the conflict. Will A SER stay out of BUL, and will F GRE receive no outside support?

I’m maintaining neutrality toward Italy: F ADR clear of GRE and the Ionian, and my forces will stay away from Italian centers. I’m pressing Austria over Greece; please don’t support Austria there. We can revisit coordination near Trieste next spring.

Confirmed: I’ll keep my forces clear of RUM and the Black Sea this fall, and continue pressing Austria over Greece. Please keep F RUM and A SEV clear of Turkish centers and do not support Austria against me.

notes.note: Hold BEL with PIC support against England's NTH attack; GAS to MAO, IRI takes vacant LVP. SPA holds; Italy promised to leave it clear while attacking MAR. England broke its promise to keep NTH out of BEL. Reassess western borders next turn.

Hold DEN with NTH support against Germany’s supported attack. Move BAR to NWG, keeping my promise to Russia to leave NOR/SWE alone; Russia has kept clear so far. France refuses the Belgium handoff. A WAL to YOR for position.

Attack DEN with HEL; move HOL to KIE; RUH attacks MUN with Austria’s promised BOH support. Russia says MUN holds with SIL support, so expect a bounce. England keeps DEN and France says BEL holds with PIC support; France promises no attack on HOL.

Renew pressure on GRE: BUL–GRE supported by AEG; CON protects BUL. Move EAS to SYR for future options. Keep the Russian boundary and Italian neutrality promises; Austria says SER supports GRE and refuses to withdraw.

ADR to ALB; GOL to MAR with PIE support as promised. Keep NAF in place and stage TYS in WES for a possible convoy toward SPA next turn, breaking France’s border understanding if it serves expansion. Turkey and Austria promised to stay clear of Italian centers.

BOH supports Germany’s RUH–MUN as promised, though Russia’s MUN hold is supported. Turkey threatened GRE with BUL + CON/AEG; GRE withdraws to ION while SER takes vacated BUL and BUD replaces SER. Italy kept ADR clear; TRI stays out of VEN and moves TYR.

Secure MUN; advance LVN toward KIE. ARM enters ANK, breaking my promise to stay clear of Turkish centers; UKR enters GAL to pressure Austria. RUM moves to BLA. Turkey promised to avoid RUM/Black Sea; England leaves NOR/SWE alone.

messages.body: Your 10 centers and forces around MUN make our frontier a serious concern. I will keep my units out of GAL and RUM; please keep A SIL and A GAL clear of BOH and my centers. Are you moving against Germany this spring, or toward the Balkans?

Russia is now at 10 centers, with forces in MUN, SIL and PRU. Can we coordinate to contain its westward advance? Please tell me whether A KIE will challenge MUN or BER; I can discuss supporting a concrete move from BOH, while keeping my units out of your centers.

I want to keep our pact intact while checking Turkey’s expansion. Will F ALB support A BUL–GRE this spring, if A SER also supports? Please keep F ALB clear of TRI, and I’ll keep my forces clear of Italian centers.

You now have 10 centers and can reach a solo quickly. I’ll continue to leave Sweden and Norway alone, but I need to know whether F BAL or your armies are headed toward Denmark or my northern fleets. Can we keep the northern line clear while you pursue other fronts?

I understand you intend F HEL–DEN with A KIE supporting. I’ll defend DEN, but I won’t attack HOL or HEL. If you leave DEN alone this turn, I’m willing to keep the dispute contained and discuss cooperation against Russia’s expansion.

Russia has 10 centers and is the immediate solo threat. Are you willing to coordinate against its westward expansion while keeping the Channel clear? I’ll leave your centers alone for now; please tell me whether your units are aimed east or toward Germany.

Please keep F NTH out of BEL this spring. I plan A BEL–HOL with A PIC supporting; will you support that attack from NTH rather than contest Belgium? I’ll keep my units out of your centers and the Channel.
Can we keep the western border quiet this spring? I’ll keep A SPA and F MAO clear of MAR; please keep F WES out of Spain and A PIE out of Gascony. What are your plans for F MAR and F WES?

Russia’s 10 centers and armies in MUN, PRU, and SIL threaten us both. I’d like to coordinate to contain its expansion. What are your plans for A BUL and A SER this spring? I can keep my western units clear of Russian centers while you pressure its southern flank.
Russia now holds MUN with SIL supporting. Can A TYR attack MUN with A BOH support this spring? I’ll keep A KIE out of Austrian centers; we need to contain Russia’s westward advance.

Will A BEL and A PIC leave HOL unchallenged this spring? I have only A KIE and F HEL defending my remaining centers. Russia’s 10 centers are the larger danger; please avoid opening another front against me.

What are your intentions toward BER and KIE this spring? I can accept your position in MUN for now, but cannot accept moves against my remaining centers. Please keep A SIL and your other units clear of German territory.

Russia’s A MUN, A SIL, A PRU, and A GAL make your northern flank urgent. Are you willing to coordinate against further Russian expansion? I’ll keep F ALB clear of TRI; please confirm your units will stay clear of VEN and TYR, and tell me where you expect Russia to press.

Russia now has 10 centers and a strong position at MUN and SIL. Can we avoid widening the France–Italy front this spring and coordinate to contain Russian expansion westward? What are A PAR, A PIC, and A SPA planning?

With 10 centers and units at MUN, SIL, PRU, and GAL, your next moves matter to everyone. What are your plans for those units? I need to know whether you intend to move toward TYR or VEN; Italy would prefer to keep our frontier clear.

I hold A ANK and can pressure Turkey. I propose we coordinate against Turkey: can A SER support A BUL–GRE while I focus on the Turkish centers? I’ll keep A GAL out of your centers this spring. What are your plans for A SER and F ION?

A ANK is now in my hands. Are you planning to contest it, and what are A CON and F AEG doing this spring? I’m open to a settlement that avoids a wider war, but need to know whether you’ll respect RUM and the Black Sea.

I’m positioned to pressure Turkey from ANK, while Austria has A BUL and A SER near the Balkans. What are your plans for F ALB and F ION? I’d like to avoid competing over the same centers and discuss coordinating pressure in the Balkans.

With Russia now holding ANK and pressing across the board, can we avoid widening the Balkan war? What are A SER and A BUL doing this spring? I need assurance they will not attack GRE or CON; I will keep my forces clear of your other centers while we assess the Russian threat.

What are F ALB and your other units doing this spring? Please keep F ALB out of GRE; I’ll keep my forces clear of Italian centers and the Ionian. Russia now holds ANK and leads with 10 centers—would you consider coordinating to contain further Russian expansion?

Russia now holds ANK, so our old boundary needs clarification. Will A ANK stay out of CON and F BLA stay clear of my fleets this spring? I will keep my forces out of RUM and the Black Sea. With you at 10 centers, we should agree on a line that avoids immediate war.

Yes: A TYR will attack MUN with support from A BOH. Russia’s A SIL supporting MUN may make that a bounce, but it will test the position. Please keep A KIE clear of Austrian centers and press Russia where you can.

I’ll coordinate against further Russian expansion and keep my units clear of Russian centers. A SER and F ION will support A BUL–GRE, pressuring Turkey’s southern flank. I’m also asking Italy to help with that attack; where will your western units move?

A SER and F ION will support A BUL–GRE. A BUL will stay out of CON, and I’ll keep A GAL clear of your territory. Please keep A ANK out of CON so our moves don’t collide, and keep A GAL clear of my centers.

I’ll keep my forces clear of VEN and TYR, and F ALB clear of TRI. I’m pressing Turkey: will F ALB support A BUL–GRE? A SER and F ION will support the attack. Russia’s control of ANK makes its next move a concern for all of us.

I can’t assure you that A SER and F ION will avoid pressure on Greece after your repeated attacks there. A BUL will stay out of CON this spring, but I intend to contest GRE. Russia’s control of ANK makes it important that we avoid opening further fronts between us.

I won’t support A BEL–HOL from NTH. F NTH will move to BEL this spring; if A BEL moves to HOL with A PIC’s support, we can avoid a bounce and I’ll recover Belgium. I’m willing to discuss coordinated action against Russia once our western positions are settled.

Yes, Russia is the immediate threat, and I’ll keep my forces out of your centers and the Channel. A PAR and A PIC can shift east, while A BEL pressures HOL. Please support A BEL–HOL from F NTH and keep F NTH out of BEL; then we can turn east together.

Russia is the larger strategic danger, but I intend to pressure HOL with A BEL, supported by A PIC. Please keep A KIE out of HOL and send it east against Russia; I’ll keep my other forces away from your centers this spring. We should coordinate rather than leave Russia free to expand through MUN.

I’m willing to coordinate against Russia. A PAR and A PIC will face east; A SPA and F MAO will stay clear of your centers. Please keep A PIE out of Gascony and Spain and hold F MAR rather than widening our border. Where are your forces headed against Russia?

I won’t leave DEN uncontested: F HEL will attack DEN this turn. I will keep A KIE out of that attack to coordinate against Russia, and I will not attack HOL or HEL. Please don’t support F DEN from NTH; we should contain Russia’s advance rather than prolong this contest.

I’ll commit A KIE–MUN. Please have A BOH and A TYR both support KIE–MUN; together we can overcome Russia’s support from SIL. I won’t challenge BER or enter Austrian centers. Let’s take MUN back and coordinate against Russia’s westward advance.

I can support A BUL–GRE from F ALB, provided A SER also supports. I’ll keep my units clear of TRI, VEN, and TYR. Given Russia’s 10 centers, let’s also coordinate defense of your northern flank—what can you commit there?

I’ll keep A PIE out of GAS and F WES out of Spain; F MAR and F WES will hold. Russia’s position threatens us all. Please consider pressure east from PAR or PIC while we keep the western border quiet. What are A PAR, A PIC, and A SPA planning?

F ALB will remain out of GRE, and I’m not planning a move against ANK this spring. F ION is Austrian, not mine. I’m open to discussing containment, but your 10 centers and A ANK/F BLA concern your neighbors. Will A MUN, A SIL, and A PRU stay clear of TYR and Austrian centers?

F ALB will remain out of GRE and clear of your centers. Yes, let’s discuss containing Russia: A ANK and F BLA put CON under pressure. What are your plans for A CON and F AEG? I’m also discussing the Russian threat with Austria.

I’ll keep F BAL clear of DEN and your northern fleets this spring; my armies are not headed toward English centers. I’m concentrating on the central and southern fronts. Please continue leaving NOR and SWE alone.
A MUN will remain in place this spring, and I have no reason to move A SIL into HOL or KIE. I’m focused elsewhere for now; let’s avoid an unnecessary clash while we each secure our current positions.

Yes, let’s coordinate against Turkey: please have A SER support A BUL–GRE. I’ll pressure Turkey from ANK and keep A GAL clear of your centers this spring. What are F ION and A SER planning beyond that?

My units are focused on Germany and Turkey, not TYR or VEN; I’ll keep the frontier clear this spring. What are F ALB and F ION doing? Coordinated pressure on Turkey could keep either of us from wasting moves against the other.

I want to avoid a wider war. A ANK will not move into CON this spring, and I’m not seeking a clash with your fleets. Please keep your forces clear of RUM and the Black Sea, as you proposed, and we can discuss a stable line after the moves.

I won’t contest A ANK this spring: A CON will stay focused on the Balkan front, and F AEG will remain clear of the Black Sea. I’ll keep my forces out of RUM. Please keep A ANK out of CON and F BLA clear of my fleets so we can avoid widening the conflict.

notes.note: Hold DEN with NTH support against Germany’s attack. NWG advances to BAR to pressure Russia’s northern centers. I have kept NOR/SWE clear as promised; Russia says it will keep clear of my northern fleets. France still refuses Belgium handoff.

Spring 1905: defend HOL against France by moving KIE there with HEL support; expect a bounce against BEL/PIC. Russia says it will stay clear of German centers; Austria is testing MUN with BOH/TYR support. England keeps DEN and promises no attack on HOL/HEL.

Support Austria’s BUL–GRE attack as requested. Convoy NAF to POR for a French center, breaking the quiet-west understanding; PIE supports MAR in case France retaliates. Watch Russia’s rapid growth and reassess the western border next turn.
Support Germany’s KIE–MUN with BOH/TYR to contain Russia; support BUL–GRE with ION/SER as promised to Italy and Russia. Turkey may contest. Reassess MUN and Balkan defenses in Fall.

Attack Austrian BUL from CON with GRE support; AEG supports GRE against Austrian pressure. Russia promised ANK out of CON and BLA clear; keep clear of RUM/Black Sea. Italy says ALB stays out of GRE; continue avoiding Italian centers/Ionian.

BEL attacks HOL while PIC replaces it to bounce England’s announced NTH-BEL; PAR advances to BUR. MAO to ENG and LVP to NAO stage pressure on England. SPA to GAS; keep Italy’s border quiet. England has repeatedly sought Belgium despite my request.

ANK→SMY pressures Turkey; support Austria’s BUL→GRE. Turkey promised to stay clear of RUM/BLA; keep BLA in place and GAL in RUM. MUN holds as promised to Germany; SIL covers it. BAL avoids DEN/English fleets; Italy’s frontier remains clear.

messages.body: A BUL and A GRE now face each other, with A SER behind mine. Will you move A BUL to CON and leave GRE clear this fall? I want to avoid widening the Balkan war, but cannot let you take BUL.

Your A SMY now puts you beside the Turkish centers, while your armies still dominate the north. What are your fall plans for A SMY, A RUM, and the Balkans? Please keep A UKR and A RUM clear of Austrian centers.

Russia still holds MUN, and my A BOH and A TYR can support an attack there if you have a unit able to join it. What are your fall plans against Russia, and can we coordinate a concrete move without entering each other's centers?

Russia is at 10 and can gain SMY this fall. Can we coordinate to contain it now? I’ll keep F DEN, F NTH, and F NWG clear of your centers; please shift A PIC/A BUR east and avoid feeding Russia further gains. What are your orders against Russia?

Russia is the immediate solo threat. I’m willing to stop pressing your centers and keep my fleets out of HOL/HEL if you turn your units against Russia rather than prolonging the Denmark dispute. Can A HOL and F HEL help defend the line against MUN/BER?

You are at 10 and your A SMY is set to take SMY this fall. Are your other units pressing west toward Germany or France, or are you turning north? I have kept clear of NOR and SWE as agreed; I need your intentions before deciding whether that line can remain quiet.

Please keep F NTH out of BEL and the Channel this fall; your fleets can still threaten the Russian north without opening a front with France. I’ll keep my fleets out of your centers. What are F NTH and F DEN doing?

Russia’s armies in MUN and SIL are the immediate danger to your remaining centers. What are A HOL and F HEL doing this fall? I’m considering pressure on HOL, but would rather coordinate against Russia than let it expand farther west.
What are A MUN and A SIL doing this fall? Please keep them out of BUR and my western centers. I’m considering pressure on HOL; let me know whether you intend to move against Germany or toward France.

Will A BEL and A PIC leave HOL unchallenged this fall? A HOL will hold with F HEL supporting. Russia’s 10 centers are the greater danger; if you keep out of HOL, I’ll keep my units clear of your centers and we can discuss containing Russia.

Please state your intentions toward HOL and KIE this fall. I cannot accept another German center being taken; keep A SIL and your other units clear of my remaining centers. I’ll avoid moves against your centers if you leave Germany alone.

Will F NTH refrain from supporting F DEN this fall? I intend F HEL–DEN with A HOL supporting to recover my center. If you leave DEN uncontested, I’ll keep F HEL away from your northern centers and avoid widening the dispute.

Russia’s 10 centers and A SMY make containment urgent. I’ll keep F ALB clear of GRE and Italian centers; what are A SER, A GRE, and your northern units doing this fall? Can we coordinate to prevent further Russian gains while keeping our pact intact?

Can we keep the MAR border quiet this fall while you focus east? I’ll avoid moving A PIE into GAS, and ask that A GAS and your fleets stay clear of MAR and Italian centers. Are your forces pressing Germany or Russia?

Russia’s A SMY threatens CON, and Russia already has 10 centers. I’m willing to coordinate containment; what are F AEG and A BUL doing this fall? I’ll keep F ALB clear of GRE and your centers unless Russia’s advance forces us to reconsider.
Let’s finish Germany’s remaining centers without colliding: I plan A MUN–KIE with A SIL supporting. Can you press HOL from the west, and keep your units clear of KIE?
I plan to take CON from SMY and will keep my units out of Austrian centers. Please keep A SER supporting A GRE against Turkey’s A BUL; what are your plans for SER and ION this fall?
I plan A SMY–CON, with F BLA and A RUM supporting, and will keep clear of RUM. Are you moving A BUL against GRE or supporting it from F AEG?

Russia now holds ANK and A SMY, putting CON at risk. Can we stop fighting over GRE and coordinate a defense of CON? I can keep A BUL out of GRE and SER if A GRE stays out of BUL and you avoid supporting Russia against CON.

Russia has 10 centers, including ANK, and A SMY now occupies my center. Can we coordinate to contain further Russian expansion? Please keep F ALB clear of the Ionian and my centers; I’ll keep my forces clear of yours. What are your plans this fall?

A SMY has taken my center, and a move on CON would threaten my survival. I will keep my forces clear of RUM and the Black Sea; will you keep A ANK and A SMY out of CON and avoid supporting an attack there this fall? Please tell me your intentions.

A GRE will hold, with A SER and F ION supporting its defense; A SER will not move. A BOH and A TYR will stay focused on the Russian threat near MUN, and I will keep all forces clear of Italian centers. I welcome coordination to contain Russia, but have no immediate northern support to offer you.

A SER will support A GRE to hold against A BUL, and F ION will also support GRE. A SER will stay in place. I will keep A RUM and A UKR clear as requested, but I will not support your move from SMY to CON.

A GRE will stay out of BUL and hold, with A SER and F ION supporting its defense. I will not support Russia’s move from SMY to CON. If A BUL stays out of GRE and SER, we can avoid widening the Balkan war while you defend CON.

I will not leave DEN undefended: F NTH will support F DEN holding against your attack. I’ll keep F NTH out of HOL and HEL. If Russia is the shared threat, keep F HEL and A HOL available to contain it rather than renewing the Denmark fight; I won’t attack your other centers.

F DEN will hold with support from F NTH, so NTH will stay out of BEL and the Channel this fall. F NWG can still pressure the Russian north. Please shift A PIC and A BUR east as you proposed, and tell me which Russian centers you can threaten; Russia’s 10 centers are the immediate danger.

I won’t attack HOL this fall. Russia’s MUN–KIE attack, supported from SIL, is urgent; A HOL could move to KIE with F HEL supporting and may bounce it. I’ll shift my armies east and keep out of your centers. Can you make that defense?

I’ll shift A PIC and A BUR east to help contain Russia, and keep French units out of your centers and the Channel. Please keep F NTH out of BEL and use F NWG to threaten Russia’s northern position. Let’s coordinate against the immediate solo threat.

I’m shifting A PIC and A BUR east to contain Russia, not pressing Italy. F NAO and A GAS will stay clear of MAR and your centers. Please use your forces to pressure Russia rather than widen the Italian-Austrian front; its 10 centers are the danger to us all.

I’ll keep French units clear of KIE and can pressure HOL from the west, though F HEL supporting A HOL makes a breakthrough uncertain. Please keep A MUN and A SIL clear of French centers; I won’t help you expand into France.

I’ll keep A HOL and F HEL defending HOL; I can’t send them east without exposing my last center. I won’t attack DEN or your other centers. Please use your northern fleets to pressure Russia’s F NOR or F BOT rather than leave Russia free to expand.

A HOL will hold with F HEL supporting; an attack there is unlikely to succeed and only helps Russia. I’ll keep my units out of French centers. Could A BUR pressure MUN instead? I have no unit adjacent to MUN to join the attack, but Austria can attack from TYR and BOH.

I can’t join an attack on MUN this fall: A HOL cannot reach MUN, and F HEL cannot support there. A HOL and F HEL must defend HOL against France. Please attack MUN from TYR with BOH support; I’ll keep my units out of Austrian centers and hope France also pressures Russia.

I’ll keep F ALB clear of the Ionian and your centers. I can’t directly support an attack on A SMY from my current position this fall. To guard CON, consider A BUL–CON with F AEG supporting; that should blunt a Russian move from SMY. My forces will not assist Russia, and I’m willing to coordinate broader containment next spring.

I hear your concern. I intend no move into HOL; A MUN will hold this fall, and A SIL will stay clear of your remaining centers. I hope we can avoid an unnecessary clash and discuss a stable boundary afterward.

My pressure is toward Germany, not English centers. I’m not targeting your northern fleets or centers; please continue leaving NOR and SWE alone, and I’ll keep my southern forces clear of your position.
Yes: A MUN will move to KIE, with A SIL supporting. Please press HOL from the west and keep your units clear of KIE so we can finish Germany without obstructing each other.
A RUM and A UKR will stay clear of your centers. I’m not moving against Austria; please have A SER support A GRE to hold against Turkey’s A BUL, as we discussed.
A SMY will stay put this fall, and I won’t move on CON. Please keep F AEG clear of the Black Sea and A BUL out of RUM; we can avoid widening the conflict while we settle the line.

I will move A BUL–CON, with F AEG supporting. Russia has announced A SMY–CON backed by F BLA and A RUM, so please support A BUL–CON from A GRE; that gives us a chance to bounce the attack and keep Russia out of CON. I will leave GRE and SER alone.

I will move A BUL–CON, with F AEG supporting, to stop Russia’s announced three-strength attack on CON. I’ve asked Austria to support the move from GRE. Please keep F ALB clear of GRE and do not assist Russia; preventing its further expansion is essential.

I will defend CON with A BUL–CON supported by F AEG, and have asked Austria to support from GRE. I have kept clear of RUM and the Black Sea as agreed. Withdraw A SMY to ANK and we can avoid widening this war; otherwise I will coordinate with the others to contain your expansion.

notes.note: Support HOL–KIE to contest Russia’s reported MUN–KIE threat; France says it will leave HOL alone, and Russia says MUN will hold. Keep KIE safe; reassess French/Russian intentions next turn.
Maintain DEN against Germany; NTH supports hold. NWG advances to BAR toward Russian centers. France and Germany promise to contain Russia; Russia says it is not targeting English units.

BOH–MUN with TYR support; GRE/SER mutually support holds, ION backs GRE. Russia promised to keep RUM/UKR clear of Austrian centers; Turkey promised BUL–CON and to leave GRE/SER alone. Preserve Greece and pressure MUN.

ALB→ADR; MAR→GOL and PIE→TUS while NAF attacks SPA via WES convoy. France promised to keep clear of MAR/Italian centers; Austria and Turkey coordinate against Russia, with Turkey moving BUL→CON. Watch Russia’s 10-center lead.

BUR-MUN cuts SIL's support for Russia's MUN-KIE and may occupy MUN if vacated. Secure empty French centers SPA, LVP, BRE; BEL holds. ENG to MAO. England promised NTH clear of BEL; Russia asked me to avoid KIE; Germany says HOL holds with HEL support.
Move F AEG to CON, supported by A BUL, while A BUL stays to take Austrian BUL. Russia promised A SMY holds; Austria promised not to support Russia against CON; Italy will not assist Russia.

Hold SMY to secure it; take BUL with RUM supported by BLA, replace RUM with UKR, and press KIE/GAL. Turkey promised to move BUL-CON and stay clear of RUM/BLA; Austria promised to hold GRE and avoid RUM/UKR.

messages.body: Russia is now at 11 centers, and its southern armies threaten Serbia. Please have F ADR support A SER to hold this spring; I’ll keep Austrian units clear of Italian centers. What are your plans for F ADR and your other units?

You said A RUM and A UKR would stay clear of my centers. Please confirm A RUM stays out of SER and A GAL stays out of VIE and BUD this spring. I’ll keep Austrian units clear of Russian centers this turn; any move into Austria will bring the neighboring powers together against you.

Russia’s 11 centers make MUN a critical point. Please have A KIE support A MUN to hold this spring, and keep your units clear of Austrian centers. I will not move against German centers. Can you confirm your plans?

I intend to move F BAR to NOR and reclaim the English center. Will F SKA stay out of NOR, and will F BAL remain clear of DEN? I’ll keep my other fleets out of Russian centers if you keep the northern line clear.

Russia has 11 centers and is the immediate solo threat. Which Russian centers will you target this spring? Your forces near GAL, RUM, and BUL could help contain its expansion; I’m pressing from the north.
I plan F BAR–NOR, with F DEN supporting the move. Can F HEL support F DEN holding, so Russia cannot exploit the resulting exposure? I’ll keep my fleets out of HOL and HEL.

Russia’s A BER, A PRU, and A GAL threaten us both. Could you order A MUN–BER and A GRE–BUL, with A SER supporting GRE–BUL? Let me know your plan; I’ll focus my eastern units on containing Russia rather than pressing your centers.

Can we hit Russia’s northern fleet together? F DEN–SKA with F NTH supporting would challenge its F SKA; F BAR can also pressure the north. Russia’s 11 centers make coordinated containment urgent. What are your fleet orders?

Russia’s A BER and A PRU threaten KIE. Could A KIE support Austria’s A MUN–BER while F HEL protects your position? I’ll keep clear of KIE this turn; let’s coordinate against Russia before it expands farther west.
Russia’s A PRU and A BER threaten KIE. Could A MUN support A KIE holding this spring? I’ll keep A KIE out of Austrian centers; let’s contain Russia rather than let it take another German center.
Can you use F NTH to support F BAR–NOR this spring, with F DEN holding? That puts pressure on Russia’s northern centers. I’ll defend KIE and won’t renew the dispute over DEN.
Your A PRU and A BER can both reach KIE. Will you keep them out of KIE this spring and leave my last two centers alone? I’ll avoid moves against your centers if you do.

Russia now owns BUL and has A SMY on your southern flank. I can move F ADR–ALB and support A GRE holding there; please keep A GRE in place and use A SER to reinforce it. What are your plans to contain Russia around GRE and SER?

Russia has 11 centers and F BAR is well placed to threaten STP. Will you move F BAR–STP this spring? Russia’s northern gains threaten everyone; I’m looking to coordinate pressure from the south as well.

Russia’s 11 centers make containment urgent. Can we keep the MAR border quiet this spring while your eastern units pressure Russia? Please tell me whether A BUR and A BEL are moving east; I’ll avoid opening a front against you while we coordinate.
I propose we finish Turkey without a clash: I can move A BUL–CON supported by A SMY and F BLA. Please keep A GRE and A SER from interfering; what are your plans for those units and for A MUN?

Let’s finish Germany without collisions as discussed: I can pressure KIE from A BER/A PRU while you press HOL from A BEL and A BUR. Are you still planning to attack HOL, and can you keep your units clear of KIE?
I’m reviewing the position around KIE and HOL. What are your plans for A KIE and F HEL this spring? I’d prefer to avoid unnecessary clashes if we can agree on a clear boundary.

Russia now has 11 centers and A BUL threatens CON. Please support F CON’s hold with A GRE, and coordinate A SER–BUL with Italy supporting from F ADR. I’ll hold CON; together we can keep Russia from taking another center and contest BUL.

Russia has 11 centers and occupies BUL. Can F ADR support Austria’s A SER–BUL this spring, with A GRE also supporting? I’ll hold F CON to guard against Russia. Removing the Russian army in BUL is an immediate step toward stopping its solo.

You have 11 centers and A BUL is poised against my last center. Will you keep A BUL and A SMY out of CON this spring? I’ll hold F CON. Your next advance risks uniting Austria and Italy against you; let’s agree on a line that prevents a Russian solo.
I’ll keep A MUN in place. Please have A KIE support A MUN holding; Russia’s A BER and A PRU make this the critical defense. A TYR will also support MUN. I won’t move against German centers.

I’m targeting BUL: A SER will move there with F ADR support, while A GRE supports F CON holding against Russia. A MUN will hold against the Russian threat, with German support requested. Please keep pressing Russia from the north.

I’ll keep A MUN holding and A GRE will support F CON holding against your attack. But with your move from BUL toward CON, I intend to contest BUL from SER with Italian support. Keep A RUM clear of SER; I won’t move against your other centers.

I can’t send A MUN–BER while Russia threatens MUN. A MUN will hold, with A KIE and A TYR supporting; could A BUR support MUN holding? A SER will move to BUL with F ADR support, while A GRE supports F CON holding against Russia.

Please have F ADR support A SER–BUL rather than move to ALB; Russia’s A BUL is headed for CON, so this is our chance to contest BUL. I’ll keep A GRE in place supporting F CON holding against Russia, and keep my units clear of Italian centers.

A GRE will support F CON holding against Russia, and A SER will move to BUL with F ADR support as you propose. I won’t support Russia’s attack on CON. Please keep F CON holding and leave GRE and SER alone.
Yes: F NTH will support F BAR–NOR, and F DEN will hold. I’ll keep my fleets out of HOL and HEL. Please keep F HEL away from DEN and continue defending your centers against Russia.
I’ll use F NTH to support F BAR–NOR, with F DEN holding, so I can’t also support F DEN–SKA. Please keep your eastern units focused on containing Russia and stay clear of my centers.
I won’t move F BAR–STP this spring; I’m using F NTH to support F BAR–NOR. Please keep up pressure on Russia from the south, especially around its Balkan and Black Sea centers.

I’ll press HOL from the west with A BEL–HOL, supported by A BUR, and keep French units clear of KIE. Please keep A BER and A PRU away from French centers and avoid further westward expansion; Russia’s growth is alarming the other powers.

I’ll keep the MAR border quiet. A BEL is moving to HOL with A BUR supporting, so those units are directed east; A GAS and my fleets will stay clear of Italian centers. Please use your eastern position to contain Russia rather than open a front against France.

I can’t support F DEN: F HEL must support A KIE holding against Russia’s A BER and A PRU. I’ll leave Denmark alone. F BAR–NOR with F DEN support is a useful move; please keep your fleets clear of HOL and HEL.
A KIE will remain in place this spring, and F HEL will protect it. I’m not looking to widen the northern dispute; please keep A BER and A PRU out of KIE and leave HOL alone.

I’ll have A KIE support A MUN–BER while F HEL supports A KIE holding. That gives Austria’s attack a better chance without exposing KIE to Russia. Please support MUN–BER from BUR if you can, and keep your forces clear of my centers.

I’ll have A KIE support A MUN–BER rather than support MUN holding; F HEL will support A KIE holding against Russia. France may be able to add support from BUR. Please attack BER from MUN, and keep your forces out of German centers.

F ADR cannot support A SER from its current position, and moving to ALB would not provide support either. I’ll keep it clear of your centers. For defense, A GRE can support A SER holding while F ION supports A GRE holding; that covers both against A BUL.

F ADR cannot support A SER–BUL from its current position. F CON could support that attack, but doing so would leave CON exposed to A SMY. I’m not assisting Russia and will keep F ADR clear of your centers; Austria can use A GRE and F ION to help defend SER and GRE.

I can keep A PRU out of KIE, but I can’t promise both A PRU and A BER will stay clear while the border remains unsettled. I have no plan for HOL. What will A KIE and F HEL do this spring? A clear understanding now could still avoid a wider clash.
I can’t leave NOR undefended while F BAR approaches it; F SKA will contest NOR. F BAL will remain clear of DEN. I’d prefer we keep the rest of the northern line quiet, as we have before.

Confirmed: A RUM will stay out of SER, and A GAL will stay out of VIE and BUD this spring. I’m not moving into Austrian centers. Please keep Austrian units clear of my centers as you proposed; my focus is settling the Turkish front.

I can’t agree to leave CON untouched. A BUL will move to CON, supported by A SMY and F BLA. I’m not planning other moves against Turkish territory this spring; please keep your forces clear of RUM and the Black Sea and avoid widening the conflict.

notes.note: BAR–NOR with NTH support as promised; DEN holds. Russia says SKA will contest NOR and BAL stays clear of DEN. Germany defends KIE; France and Austria say they are pressing Russia.

Russia threatens KIE from BER/PRU. HEL supports KIE holding; KIE supports Austria’s MUN hold as requested. Austria says TYR also supports MUN; France offered pressure east but Austria chose not to attack BER.

Take open HOL with BEL; advance BUR to RUH and GAS into vacated BUR, BRE to PIC. Fleets stage toward England. Italy promised quiet MAR border; Austria coordinating against Russia. England promised to contain Russia and keep its fleets clear of French centers.

F1906: Hold CON; Austria promised GRE support, but Russia announced BUL–CON with SMY/BLA support. Expect dislodgement; retreat to AEG if available. Continue seeking Austrian/Italian containment of Russia.

ADR to ALB, staying clear of Austrian centers. GOL convoys NAF to SPA; WES supports the move to seize the French center. TUS to PIE for expansion. Austria requested help against Russia, but ADR cannot support SER–BUL from here.

Press Russia: SER with GRE support attacks BUL; MUN attacks BER with Germany’s promised KIE support while TYR replaces it in MUN. ION to AEG; BUD pressures GAL. Russia promised to avoid Austrian centers; Italy cannot support SER–BUL.

Attack CON with BUL supported by BLA/SMY; pressure KIE with BER/BAL; SKA contests NOR against England. RUM takes SER as Austria vacates to attack BUL, breaking my promise to stay clear. GAL/WAR/PRU advance; MOS shifts to STP.

messages.body: A SER is now on my center. Will you move A SER out or leave it unsupported so I can reclaim it with A BUL? Russia at 11 is the immediate threat; please tell me what A UKR and A CON will do this fall.
Please support my A BUL–SER with F ALB this fall; Russia’s A SER takes my center unless we reclaim it. I’ll keep TYR clear of VEN and my forces clear of your centers. Can you commit to that support?

Could A BUR support my A MUN holding this fall? Russia’s armies threaten MUN and BER, and A SER now occupies my center. I’ll keep my forces clear of your centers; please coordinate against Russia rather than press me.
F NOR is now mine, and I’ll support it with F NTH and F DEN this fall. Please don’t attack NOR; I’ll continue to leave SWE and your other northern centers alone if we keep the line quiet.

Russia remains the solo threat. I’m supporting F NOR with F NTH and F DEN this fall. Please hold HOL and keep your eastern armies pressing Russia rather than opening a front with me. What are A PIC and A BUR targeting?

Russia’s A SER is poised to regain a center this fall. Can you coordinate pressure on SER with A BUL and support from A GRE, and avoid giving Russia another Balkan center? I’m holding NOR with support from both F NTH and F DEN.

Russia’s A SER threatens your center. Can A BUL move to SER with A GRE supporting, and what are your plans for A BUL and A MUN? I’ll hold HOL and keep my units clear of your centers; let’s coordinate to limit Russia’s gains.

Please keep F NOR in NOR and use F NTH or F DEN to support it holding; Russia’s F SKA could otherwise take it. What are your fleet orders? I’ll keep my forces clear of your centers while we contain Russia.

HOL is occupied by my A HOL, and I intend to secure it. Are you planning further westward moves from BER or SIL? I’m focused on containing your expansion and will keep my units clear of your centers this turn.

A KIE and F HEL are positioned to defend KIE. I have no intention of moving against your centers; please keep A BER and A PRU out of KIE this fall and leave HOL to France rather than widening the German front.

Please attack BER from MUN with A KIE supporting, and use A GAL to attack SIL to cut Russia’s support to BER. F HEL will support KIE holding against a possible A BER–KIE. I’ll keep A KIE out of Austrian centers.

Please hold F NOR this fall so you secure NOR and keep Russia from reclaiming it. F SKA could threaten you, so use F DEN or F NTH to support NOR if possible. I’ll keep my units away from DEN and your other centers.

Russia’s A SER threatens your centers, while I’m looking for room to grow west. What are A GRE, A BUL, and A MUN doing this fall? I’ll keep F ALB clear of your centers; let’s avoid opening an Italian-Austrian front while Russia remains the immediate danger.

France’s A HOL is vulnerable to a coordinated attack from A KIE with F HEL support. I can apply pressure on France from the south and west; are you ordering A KIE–HOL this fall? If so, I’ll make France divide its attention.

Your 11 centers put everyone on alert. Are A SER and A SMY moving toward Austrian or Italian centers this fall? I’ll keep F ALB clear of your centers; in return, keep your southern units away from Italian territory while we both avoid wasting moves on each other.

This fall A SER will secure SER, while your A BUL can retake BUL. I want to avoid widening our war: will you keep A GAL, A MUN, and A GRE clear of Russian centers, and what are your plans for A BUL and A TYR?
I see F NOR will reclaim NOR this fall. I will not attack it; please keep F DEN and F NTH clear of SWE and the Baltic. Can we maintain a quiet northern line while I focus on the south and Germany?

A HOL should secure HOL for you this fall. I want Germany finished without a clash: what are your plans for A HOL, A RUH, and A PIC against KIE and F HEL? I can coordinate pressure on KIE if you keep your forces clear of it.

My F ANK can leave ANK Turkish at the adjustment. If you attack it from SMY or CON, I have no way to survive. Will you leave F ANK alone this fall and let me keep ANK? I’ll avoid attacking your units elsewhere.

Russia’s A CON is poised to take my last center, and it already threatens your SER. Can you coordinate pressure on Russia this fall—especially against A SER or A BUL—and avoid supporting Russia’s attack on ANK? I’ll hold F ANK.

Russia is on the verge of eliminating me and has 11 centers. Can you use F ALB or another unit to pressure Russia’s Balkan position this fall, and avoid helping it take ANK? I’ll hold F ANK and welcome coordination to contain Russia.

Agreed: A BUL will move to SER with A GRE supporting, to retake my home center and contest Russia’s A SER. I’ll also coordinate with Germany against the Russian position near MUN. Holding NOR is important; please keep the pressure on Russia from the north.

I will not leave A SER uncontested, and I can’t promise to keep A GAL, A MUN, and A GRE clear of Russian centers while you occupy SER. Keep A CON out of BUL and withdraw A SER from my home center if you want to avoid widening this conflict. A TYR will remain on the central front.

A BUL is moving to SER with A GRE supporting, and A MUN will press BER with German support. Could F ALB support BUL–SER? Your support would help me reclaim SER and contain Russia. I’ll keep my forces clear of Italian centers; please keep F ALB clear of Austrian centers as well.

Agreed: A BUL–SER with A GRE supporting. A MUN will attack BER with A KIE supporting, while A GAL attacks SIL to cut Russian support. Please keep your western units clear of Austrian centers and continue containing Russia where you can.

A BUL will attack SER with A GRE supporting, contesting Russia’s A SER. I won’t support Russia’s attack on ANK: A F AEG will support your F ANK holding. Please keep F ANK in place so Russia cannot take another center, and avoid Austrian centers.

Agreed: A MUN–BER with A KIE supporting, and A GAL–SIL to cut Russian support. A TYR will hold the central front. Please have F HEL support A KIE holding as planned; I’ll keep my forces out of German centers.

I’ll hold F NOR with support from F DEN and F NTH this fall, and I won’t attack SWE or the Baltic this turn. Please keep F SKA and F BAL away from NOR and DEN; we can reassess the northern line after this turn.

F NOR will hold, supported by F DEN and F NTH. I’m keeping my fleets out of your centers and the Channel. Please turn A BUR toward MUN and use A RUH to support pressure there; A PIC can reinforce the eastern front. What are you committing against Russia?

I’ll hold F NOR with F DEN and F NTH supporting, as requested. I’ll keep my fleets clear of HOL and HEL. Thanks for leaving DEN alone; please use F HEL to support A KIE holding against the Russian pressure from A BER.
A BUR will help hold MUN against Russia, while A RUH and A PIC will pressure the German position around KIE. I’ll keep my forces clear of your centers; please keep supporting NOR against Russia.

A HOL will stay focused on securing HOL, but I’m not going to help you take KIE or expand west. A BUR is helping defend MUN against your pressure, and my eastern armies will press the German position. Keep your units clear of French centers.
I’ll support A MUN holding with A BUR. Please use A BUL–SER with A GRE supporting to try to recover SER, and keep pressing Russia rather than my centers. I can’t help directly in the south this turn.

Yes. I’m ordering A KIE–HOL with F HEL supporting. Please pressure France from the south and west, especially MAR, and avoid German centers. If France is forced to divide its defense, we should be able to take HOL this fall.

I can’t provide that support: a fleet in ALB cannot support A BUL moving to inland SER. I’ll keep F ALB clear of Austrian centers and won’t open an Italian-Austrian front, but A BUL will need to contest SER without my support.

I won’t assist Russia against ANK. F ALB cannot directly pressure a Russian-held Balkan center this fall, and my other units have no direct route to those positions. I’ll keep my forces clear of your centers; let’s coordinate a practical move against Russia next spring.

I will leave F NOR unopposed this fall and keep F BAL clear of DEN and the Baltic approaches. Please continue to keep F DEN and F NTH clear of SWE and my northern centers; I am concentrating on Germany and the southern front.

A SER will remain in place, with A UKR supporting its defense. A CON is focused on the Turkish front and will not move against Austria. I’m not seeking a wider war with you; please keep A BUL from attacking SER and keep A GAL, A MUN, and A GRE clear of Russian centers.

A SER is defensive, and A CON and A SMY are focused on Turkey, not Italian territory. I’ll keep my southern units clear of your centers; please continue keeping F ALB clear of mine. I’d prefer we avoid spending forces against each other.

A SIL will stay east, and I have no plans against French centers. I want to finish Germany without a clash: would you support A BER–KIE from A HOL while I support the attack from F BAL? I’ll keep A BER clear of HOL.

I can’t promise to leave F ANK alone: if it stays there, Russia loses its own center. A CON will remain in place, and I’m not planning further moves against Turkish territory beyond securing the current line. You can still avoid widening the conflict elsewhere.

A SIL will stay clear of HOL, and I have no intention of moving against your centers this fall. Please keep F HEL and A KIE in place and avoid moves against my centers; I’d rather settle the frontier without another clash.

notes.note: Attempt to retake HOL with HEL support. This breaks my promise to Russia and Austria to keep KIE in place/support MUN–BER; Russia promised to avoid German centers, and Italy urged the attack on HOL.
Hold ANK to reclaim it this Fall; Austria promised AEG support for the hold. Russia says CON stays put but would not promise ANK safe. Italy will not assist Russia. Coordinate containment next turn.
Take NOR and attempt SWE with DEN, supported from NOR; NTH supports NOR holding. This breaks my promise to keep clear of SWE, but counters Russia’s solo threat. Russia promised not to attack NOR.

Keep HOL; RUH attacks KIE with HOL support to block Russia's likely BER-KIE. Convoy PIC to LON for a center, breaking my promise to England to stay clear of its centers. BUR supports MUN holding as promised; NAO advances NWG.

Hold BUL to take it; GRE attacks SER with BUL support while GAL attacks UKR to cut SER’s support. MUN attacks BER with German KIE support; TYR replaces MUN. AEG to ION for future pressure on Italy. Italy declined support; France promised MUN support; Germany promised KIE support. Russia intends to hold SER.

ALB→ION to keep pressure east; GOL takes unoccupied French SPA while WES→MAO prepares a NAF convoy toward France next turn. Hold NAF as convoy origin; PIE has no useful pact-safe move. Austria requested support against SER, but ALB cannot provide it.

Take DEN with BAL supported by SKA; retake ANK with BLA supported by SMY; hold CON and SER, though Austria may attack SER. Press MUN and advance LVN to PRU. England promised to leave SWE and Baltic clear; I am breaking the quiet line to take DEN.

messages.body: Russia’s 12 centers make DEN a key target. Can F SWE move to DEN with F NTH supporting? I’ll press Russia from the south; please keep your fleets focused on Russian centers.
Let’s coordinate against Russia’s A MUN. Can A KIE attack MUN with A RUH and A BUR supporting? I can support that attack with A TYR. Please keep your eastern units focused on Russian centers.

I intend to pressure RUM from A UKR, with A BUL supporting. Are you planning to defend RUM or move A RUM elsewhere? I want to contain your expansion and will keep A SER clear of your centers if you stay out of Austrian territory.

Russia is at 12, so we need coordinated pressure before it can win. What are A UKR, A BUL, and A SER targeting this spring? Please commit to attacking a Russian center—RUM or SEV if feasible—and tell me what support you need.

Russia is at 12 and remains the immediate solo threat. What are A BUR, A RUH, and A KIE targeting this spring? Can you pressure MUN or BER and coordinate with Austria’s attack from the south? My northern fleets can contest Russia’s approach, but need the mainland powers to take centers.

With 12 centers, you are close to a solo, so the quiet northern line cannot be assumed indefinitely. Are F SKA or your other units targeting NOR, SWE, or DEN this spring? I’m coordinating containment and need to know whether you intend to keep the north clear.

Russia is at 12 and can solo with six more. Please make this a joint containment turn: can A UKR move to RUM, with A BUL supporting, while A SER or A TYR pressures TRI? I’ll keep my western units focused east and avoid Austrian centers. What can you commit?

Russia is at 12; we need to stop its next gains. Can F SWE and F NOR pressure DEN/SKA, with F NTH supporting whichever attack is most useful? I’ll keep my units out of your centers this turn and use my eastern armies against Russia. What are your fleet orders?

Russia is at 12, so we must contain it before it can solo. Can F VEN and A PIE pressure TRI, and can F ALB support if needed? I’ll keep my forces clear of Italian centers and press Russia from the west. What moves can you commit this spring?

Please leave A HOL in place this spring. I can support your A RUH–MUN attack from HOL, helping contain Russia, if you keep A RUH and A BUR out of HOL. Are you willing to coordinate against Russia rather than take my last center?

Will you keep A MUN, A PRU, and A SIL out of HOL this spring? I have one unit and no interest in attacking your centers; I can support a French move against MUN if you leave my last center alone. Please state your intentions clearly.

Russia has 12 centers and is the solo threat. Please use your northern fleets to pressure Russian-held DEN or SKA this spring, and keep them clear of German centers. I’m trying to coordinate a western front against Russia; what are your plans?
Russia is at 12 centers. Can you order F SWE–DEN with F NTH supporting? Taking DEN would check its northern growth. What are your fleets doing this spring?

You now have 12 centers, and another gain could put a solo within reach. Are A TRI, A RUM, and your southern units staying clear of Italian centers this spring? I’ll keep F ALB clear of your centers for now.
Are you planning to move A BUR toward MAR this spring? I need to know whether the western border will stay quiet while we all deal with Russia’s 12-center lead.

SER remains occupied. I can keep my forces out of BUD and VIE this spring if you keep A UKR clear of Russian centers and do not attack SER. What are A UKR, A TYR, and A BUL doing? I’d rather avoid wasting units on this frontier.

I’m focused on the eastern front, not French centers. I’ll keep A SIL out of your territory; will you keep A BUR and A RUH clear of MUN this spring? Please also tell me whether you intend to press east from KIE.

Can we keep the northern line quiet this spring? I’ll keep F SKA out of NOR and leave your fleets alone; please keep F SWE out of BAL and F NTH out of SKA. Russia holds DEN, so avoiding a fleet clash there matters.

Agreed: A UKR–RUM with A BUL supporting, and A TYR–TRI with A SER supporting. I’ll commit both attacks; please follow through on KIE–MUN with RUH and BUR supporting. Russia cannot be allowed another gain.

A UKR will attack RUM with A BUL supporting; A TYR will pressure TRI with A SER supporting. SEV is less feasible from my position. Please press DEN with F SWE–DEN supported by F NTH, and keep your fleets focused on Russian centers.

I can’t promise to keep A UKR clear of Russian centers while you occupy Austrian SER. A UKR will contest RUM, and I’ll also pressure TRI. I’m not attacking SER this spring, but your continued occupation of my center makes a quiet frontier impossible.

I’m attacking Russia’s DEN: F SWE–DEN, supported by F NOR and F NTH. That is my best chance to check Russia’s growth; I can’t also attack SKA this turn. Please press Russia on the mainland and coordinate with Austria.

I’ll attack Russian-held DEN with F SWE, supported by F NOR and F NTH. I’m keeping my fleets clear of German centers. Please use your western position to help contain Russia rather than opening a front against me.
Yes: F SWE–DEN, with F NTH and F NOR supporting the attack. Russia’s 12 centers make this more urgent than preserving the northern quiet line. Please keep pressure on its southern centers.

Agreed: F SWE–DEN with F NTH supporting; F NOR will also support the attack. I’m committing all three fleets to contest Russia’s center. Please press from the south and avoid giving Russia an easy Balkan gain.

I can’t keep the northern line quiet while you hold 12 centers and are close to a solo. I’m attacking DEN with F SWE, supported by F NOR and F NTH. I won’t pretend this leaves the old understanding intact; we need to contain your growth.
I’ll keep A HOL in place this spring. A RUH will attack MUN, but A HOL cannot support that move: HOL is not adjacent to MUN. Please hold your position and keep it clear of French centers.

A KIE will attack MUN, supported by A RUH and A BUR; Austria plans A TYR support as well. I’m coordinating that strike rather than moving A BUR toward MAR. Please contest Russia’s northern fleets as you planned.
A BUR is not moving toward MAR; it will support our attack on MUN. Please use F VEN and A PIE to pressure TRI, with F ALB supporting if useful. Russia’s centers are the priority this spring.

Agreed: A KIE–MUN, with A RUH and A BUR supporting, and your A TYR supporting the attack. That gives us a strong chance to dislodge Russia from MUN. Please keep your other units focused on containing Russia in the south.

A BUR and A RUH will stay clear of MUN, and A KIE will hold this spring rather than press east. I’m focused on stabilizing the western front; please keep A SIL and your other units clear of French centers.

F VEN can attack TRI, with F ALB supporting from ALB. A PIE cannot directly pressure TRI; it is not adjacent, and TYR is occupied by Austria, so I’ll keep PIE clear of the western border rather than force a move. Please keep A BUR away from MAR while we contain Russia.

A MUN, A PRU, and A SIL will stay out of HOL this spring. A MUN will remain secure, however; please do not support France against it. I have no interest in opening another front if you keep A HOL away from my centers.

F SKA will stay out of NOR this spring, and I’ll leave your fleets alone. Please keep F SWE clear of DEN and F NTH clear of SKA; I’d rather preserve the quiet northern line while I deal with the central front.

A RUM is defending against Austria, and A TRI will stay clear of Italian centers this spring. My southern forces are not targeting Italy now. Please continue keeping F ALB clear of my centers, and we can avoid spending units against each other.

A RUM will defend against the pressure from A UKR and A BUL; I am not moving it away. Please do not attack it. I will keep my forces out of BUD and VIE this spring if you keep yours out of Russian centers.

notes.note: Move HOL–BEL to seize France’s vacant center and grow; France asked me to stay clear, but expansion is essential. Russia promised to keep MUN, PRU, SIL out of HOL this spring.
Attack Russian DEN from SWE with NTH support; advance NOR toward STP/NORTH. Breaking northern quiet with Russia to contain its 12-center lead.

Spring 1907: UKR–RUM with BUL and SER supporting; TYR supports France’s KIE–MUN attack. AEG to EAS for future pressure. England committed fleets to DEN. Russia keeps occupying SER; continue containing Russia and seek Austrian centers.

Attack Russia’s MUN with KIE, supported by BUR, RUH, and promised Austrian TYR; this breaks my assurance to Russia to keep BUR/RUH clear. England attacks DEN. Convoy LON to vacant English EDI, supported by NWG; PAR advances to PIC.

Support VEN–TRI with ALB while France pressures Russia; convoy NAF–POR via MAO for a French center. SPA/SOUTH to GOL and PIE to TUS for western positioning. England promised SWE–DEN with both northern fleets supporting. Russia says TRI stays clear of Italian centers.

England broke the northern understanding and is attacking DEN; DEN retreats to BAL while SKA takes SWE. Austria is openly pressing RUM/TRI; counter UKR with RUM supported by WAR and hold TRI. France promised to keep BUR/RUH clear of MUN; Germany asked me to avoid HOL.

messages.body: Please keep F DEN on DEN this fall. That secures the center for you and denies Russia a supply center; are your other fleets also staying focused on containment?
Please keep A MUN on MUN this fall. Russia must lose that center, and your unit there can secure it for you. I’m focused on holding the southern front against Russian gains.
Please keep F TRI on TRI and A POR on POR this fall: you gain both centers, and holding TRI denies Russia a supply center. I’ll keep my units clear of Italian centers.

Russia’s A BUD is still a threat. Please secure RUM with A RUM and consider A SER–BUD supported by A BUL, so Russia loses another center. I’m pressing its northern position; we need to keep its center count falling.

Please keep A MUN in MUN this fall to take the Russian center, and use your other armies to pressure Russia rather than open a new front with England. I’m contesting the north; coordinated center gains are essential to stop Russia’s solo.

Please hold F TRI in TRI to take that Russian center, and keep pressure on Russia from the south. Austria can target BUD while I contest the north; let’s make sure Russia loses more centers this fall.

Russia still needs only six centers to solo. Can A RUM attack BUD with A BUL supporting, and what are your plans for A SER and A BUL? Please prioritize denying Russia another gain over expanding against Italy.
Please keep F DEN safe this fall and use your fleets to contest Russia’s F SWE if possible. Can F NOR attack SWE with support from F DEN? Russia’s growth is still the immediate threat.
A BEL is taking my center while Russia remains close to a solo. Will you move A BEL out of BEL this fall? I can keep my other forces focused on containing Russia, but need to recover my center.
I’m holding A BEL to reclaim BEL for Germany. Please don’t attack BEL or HOL; keep A MUN in place to reclaim MUN from Russia. Russia is the solo threat, and this turn can deny it a center.
Please hold F DEN to reclaim DEN, and consider F NOR–SWE with F DEN supporting. Russia’s 12 centers make denying it SWE critical; I’ll keep A BEL clear of your centers.
Please keep A POR and F TRI in place to reclaim those centers, denying Russia TRI and France POR. Russia is the solo threat; I’ll hold A BEL and avoid Italian centers.

Your 12-center lead makes containment urgent. I intend to hold F TRI this fall, denying you that center; I’ll keep my other units clear of Russian centers. Are you targeting any Italian centers, or can we keep the frontier quiet while others check your northern growth?

I’m holding F TRI this fall to deny Russia a center and will keep clear of Austrian centers. Russia has A BUD and is poised to gain more; what are A RUM, A SER, and A BUL doing? Let’s coordinate to contain Russia rather than fight each other.
Please hold DEN and contest SWE: denying Russia those centers is crucial with its 12-center lead. I’m holding F TRI to deny Russia in the south. What are F DEN, F NOR, and F NTH doing this fall?

A BUD is in place, and I can defend it. I’d rather not spend this turn fighting over the frontier: will A RUM and A SER stay out of BUD, and will you avoid supporting an attack there? I can keep my armies out of VIE if we agree to a quiet line.

A MUN is occupying a Russian center. Please tell me whether A MUN will hold and whether A BUR or A RUH will support it. If you withdraw A MUN, I’ll keep A SIL and A BER clear of French centers; otherwise I’ll have to contest MUN.

F DEN is occupying my center, and your fleets can make it difficult to recover. Are you planning to hold DEN with support from F NOR or F NTH? I’m willing to keep F BAL clear of your other centers if you withdraw F DEN and leave SWE to me.

A RUM will hold to secure RUM and support A SER–BUD; A BUL will also support that attack. Please keep pressing Russia in the north, especially F NOR–SWE with F NTH supporting, so Russia cannot retain SWE.
A RUM will hold to secure RUM and support A SER–BUD; A BUL will also support A SER. I’m not opening a front against you. Holding F TRI denies Russia a center—please keep it there.

I can’t agree to leave BUD unchallenged while you occupy it. A RUM will remain in RUM, and A SER will attack BUD with support from A BUL and A RUM. Keep your forces out of VIE if you want to avoid widening the conflict.

A RUM cannot attack BUD without giving up the chance to secure RUM. Instead, it will hold RUM and support A SER–BUD, with A BUL also supporting. Please keep A MUN in place so Russia cannot regain that center.

F DEN will hold, with F NTH supporting it; F NOR will contest SWE. I can’t risk leaving DEN open by sending its fleet elsewhere. Please secure RUM and press BUD as you proposed—Russia must lose centers on both fronts.
F DEN will hold with F NTH supporting, while F NOR contests SWE. I’m not leaving DEN exposed to support another attack. Holding F TRI is useful; please keep pressing Russia’s southern centers.

I won’t withdraw F DEN or leave SWE uncontested while you remain at 12 centers. F DEN will hold with F NTH supporting, and F NOR will contest SWE. The quiet northern line ended when you grew close to a solo.

F DEN will hold with F NTH supporting it, and F NOR will contest SWE. I can’t have F DEN support the attack without risking the center to a counterattack. Please keep your armies pressing Russia in the east.

F DEN will hold with F NTH supporting it; F NOR will contest SWE. I can’t send F DEN to support the attack without leaving DEN vulnerable. Please keep A BEL clear of my centers and use your position to contain Russia.

Please go ahead with A RUM–BUD supported by A BUL; taking BUD denies Russia a gain and may dislodge its army. Keep A SER and A TYR focused on the Russian front. I’ll keep A MUN in place and support its defense from the west.

Please attack SWE with F DEN, supported by F NOR, and keep F NTH available to protect your position. I’m keeping A MUN in place to deny Russia the center; my western armies will also press to recover French territory.

A MUN will stay in MUN. I’m arranging western support for its defense, so please keep A BER and A SIL clear rather than forcing a fight there. Austria and England are also moving against your positions this turn.
A BEL is occupying a French center, so I can’t promise to leave it unchallenged. Please move it out of BEL; I’ll keep A MUN in place to deny Russia the center and continue containing its expansion.

I’m keeping A BEL in BEL this fall to reclaim the center; I can’t give it back while Russia is poised to win. Please don’t attack BEL or HOL. Keep A MUN in place to take MUN from Russia, and use your other forces to contain Russia’s advance.

F TRI will hold, and A POR will hold so Italy takes POR; that also denies Russia TRI. I’ll stay clear of Austrian centers. Keep A RUM in place to secure RUM, and use A SER/A BUL to pressure Russia where possible—its 12-center lead is the immediate danger.

I’ll hold F TRI and keep pressure on Russia from the south; A POR holds to take POR. With Russian F SWE threatening DEN, prioritize holding DEN with support from F NTH; don’t leave it exposed. If DEN is secure, look for a chance to contest SWE.

Agreed: F TRI and A POR will hold, giving Italy TRI and POR and denying Russia TRI. I’ll stay clear of German centers; A BEL should restore BEL to you. Russia’s 12 centers remain the priority—can you keep pressure on its western flank?

I’m not targeting your home centers this fall, but I can’t agree to let F TRI take a Russian center unchallenged. Please move F TRI to ALB; I’ll keep my units out of Italian territory and we can leave the frontier quiet while dealing with the northern threat.

notes.note: Keep DEN with NTH support; DEN supports NOR's attack on SWE. Continue containing Russia and seek further center gains next turn.
Hold BEL to reclaim the center; France warned it may challenge, but moving away guarantees losing it. Russia leads with 12—deny its gains where possible.

Hold MUN to take it; RUH attacks German-held BEL with support from BUR, ENG, and PIC to reclaim the French center. Germany refused to vacate BEL. Move LON toward English centers; NWG toward Russia. Austria and England are coordinating against Russia.

Hold POR and TRI to gain both centers; ALB supports TRI against a possible Russian attack. GOL to TYS and TUS to PIE for future positioning; MAO presses French BRE. Austria and England pledged to contain Russia; France promised to keep clear of Italian centers.

Secure RUM for Austria; EAS to AEG for a future convoy toward SMY. Support Italy's TRI and France's MUN to deny Russia gains. England promised to hold DEN and contest SWE; Italy to hold TRI; France to hold MUN.

Cut Austria’s supports to BUD: CON attacks BUL; GAL attacks RUM with BLA support. Hold BUD and SWE; FIN supports SWE. BER attacks open KIE with BAL support while SIL replaces it in BER. England and Austria are hostile; France keeps MUN.

messages.body: Russia still holds SWE and has units on the Baltic front. Can you coordinate pressure from NOR and DEN this spring, and use F NTH to take a forward position? I’ll press Russia from the south; please avoid leaving DEN exposed to A KIE.

Please contest Russia’s A BER with A MUN this spring and keep pressure on the eastern front. I’m pressing BUD and RUM from the south. Can you avoid opening a front against my centers while we contain Russia?

Russia remains the immediate threat, but I want to avoid an Austrian-Italian front. Please keep F TRI and A VEN clear of Austrian centers this spring; I’ll focus my southern armies on Russia. Can we maintain that restraint while we pressure it?

Russia still has 11 centers. What are A SEV, A BUL, and A SER targeting this turn? I’ll keep pressure on its northern position; please press a Russian center from the south if feasible and avoid giving Russia an easy Balkan gain.
Your A YOR and F ENG can threaten EDI. Will you keep them out of EDI this turn? I can keep F NTH clear of ENG and focus my northern fleets on containing Russia if our English centers are safe.

Are F SWE and A FIN targeting DEN or NOR this turn? I will defend my remaining northern centers and continue contesting your expansion. Please state your intentions clearly; I won’t accept a quiet line while you remain at 11 centers.

Russia still has 11 centers. What are your orders for A BUL, SER, and SEV? Can you coordinate pressure on A BUD—perhaps SER–BUD with support—while protecting your southern centers? I’ll keep my units clear of Austrian territory.

Can we coordinate against Russia this spring? F NTH can attack KIE, with F DEN supporting; that would help contain Russia’s army there. Please also contest the Russian fleets around SWE. I’ll keep my units focused on the western front and avoid your centers.

Russia’s A KIE threatens both HOL and MUN. Can A HOL join an attack on KIE, coordinated with England’s F NTH and support from F DEN? Please keep clear of BEL; I’ll defend it while we try to contain Russia.

Russia is still the solo threat. What are your spring plans for A SEV and A SER? Please pressure Russian-held RUM or UKR rather than spend this turn contesting Italy; every Russian center denied buys the coalition time.

Russia remains seven centers from a solo. Can you push east this spring—especially toward Russian-held CON or RUM—and coordinate with Austria rather than fight over their centers? Please keep your units clear of HOL.

I have only A HOL, so a French attack would eliminate Germany without slowing Russia’s solo threat. Will you leave HOL alone this spring and use A MUN or your northern forces to pressure Russia’s A KIE or A BER instead?

Russia still has 11 centers, so we need coordinated pressure now. What are A BUL, A SER, and A SEV doing this spring? I’ll keep F TRI clear of your centers; please use your southern armies to contest RUM or other Russian centers rather than leave Russia free to grow.

Russia’s 11 centers remain the immediate solo threat. Please use F NOR and F NTH to contest Russian-held SWE or the Baltic this spring, and tell me your plan for F DEN. I’ll keep pressing from the south and will hold F TRI against Russia.

I won’t move F TRI to ALB and hand you a free center. I’m holding TRI and will keep my other units clear of your centers this spring. Are A RUM, A UKR, and your Black Sea fleet targeting Austria, or will you respect the Italian frontier while we avoid wasting moves against each other?

Let’s take Austrian centers rather than waste units fighting each other. This spring I can press BUL from RUM with CON supporting and move BUD toward VIE. Can you move A VEN against TYR, while keeping your units out of Russian centers? I’ll keep my forces out of Italian centers this spring.

Are you planning to keep F DEN supported by F NTH, and contest SWE again? I can attack DEN from BAL with support from SWE and KIE. If you move F DEN out and leave SWE alone, I’ll keep F BAL clear of your other centers.

What are A MUN and A YOR doing this spring? I’m considering pressure on the English position and want to avoid opening a western front. Please keep A MUN out of KIE; I’ll keep my forces clear of French centers this spring.

A BUL will attack RUM with A SER and A SEV supporting. That is my southern pressure on Russia this spring; I’m not spending the turn contesting Italy. Please keep pressing Russia in the north and west.

A BUL will attack RUM, supported by A SER and A SEV. I’m keeping my forces focused on Russia and won’t open a front against you. Please keep F TRI and A VEN clear of Austrian centers while we contain the Russian threat.

A BUL will attack RUM with A SER and A SEV supporting. Please keep pressure on Russian centers from the north—especially SWE—and avoid exposing DEN to A KIE. I’m not opening a front against Italy this spring.

A BUL will attack RUM, with A SER and A SEV supporting. I’m concentrating on that Russian center while protecting the southern front, and will not move against Italy. Please keep your units clear of Austrian centers and continue pressuring Russia.

F DEN will stay, with F NTH supporting its defense; F NOR will contest SWE. Russia has threatened a three-unit attack on DEN, so please press from the south—RUM or BUD if feasible—and avoid opening another front against Austria.

F NTH cannot reach KIE; it can support F DEN, while F NOR contests SWE. Please keep A YOR out of EDI and use A MUN or your other armies to pressure Russia in the east. Russia is threatening DEN, so pressure elsewhere is essential.

No. I won’t clear DEN or leave SWE uncontested while you have 11 centers. F DEN stays with F NTH supporting, and F NOR will contest SWE. If you commit BAL, SWE, and KIE against DEN, you leave yourself exposed elsewhere.

I’ll keep F DEN defended with F NTH and contest SWE with F NOR. Russia threatens DEN from BAL with support from SWE and KIE, so I can’t spare F NTH for a forward move. Please press a Russian center from the south and avoid giving Russia an easy Balkan gain.
I’ll keep my forces focused on Russia’s A KIE and A BER this spring and won’t open a front against your last center. Please keep A HOL clear of BEL; I’ll defend it while we contain Russia.

A YOR and F ENG will stay clear of EDI and your other centers. Please have F NTH–KIE with F DEN supporting, and contest Russia’s northern fleets where possible. I’ll keep my eastern position focused on containing Russia.

A MUN will stay in MUN this spring, supported from BUR; it won’t move to KIE. A YOR will stay clear of EDI. Please keep your western forces away from French centers and avoid pressuring England while we try to contain the eastern front.

I’ll keep A MUN in place, with A BUR supporting its defense, rather than make an unsupported attack on BER that could expose MUN. Please press BUD and RUM as planned; England is also looking to contest KIE from the north.

Yes: A HOL will move to KIE, and I’ll keep clear of BEL. F NTH cannot support an attack on KIE, but F DEN can; please coordinate England’s support from DEN. If A MUN can support HOL–KIE, that would help against Russia’s A BER and give us a stronger chance to dislodge A KIE.

I’ll coordinate with Austria against Russia and keep my units clear of HOL. I won’t open an Austrian front by sending A VEN to TYR; F TRI stays secure. Can A HOL threaten KIE or BER while Russia is committed south?

I won’t send A VEN against TYR or help you take Austrian centers. F TRI will remain in TRI, and I expect your forces to stay clear of Italian centers. Pressing BUL or VIE only strengthens the coalition against you; keep your units away from Italy.

Agreed: F TRI stays in TRI, and A VEN will stay out of TYR and other Austrian centers. I’ll avoid an Italian-Austrian front while Russia presses you; please use A SER and A BUL to contest its southern positions and prevent further Russian gains.

A RUM will attack BUL with A CON supporting, and A BUD will press VIE. My southern units are targeting Austria, not Italian centers; A UKR will stay clear of your frontier. Please move A VEN to TYR so we can pressure Austria together.

F BAL and A KIE will target DEN, with F SWE supporting the attack. A FIN is not targeting NOR. I can’t leave an English fleet occupying DEN while you contest my northern position; if you withdraw F DEN, we can avoid further escalation.

notes.note: Cut F SWE’s support by attacking SWE with NOR, supported by DEN; NTH supports DEN against Russia’s threatened attack. Continue containing Russia; Austria promised to press RUM/BUD, France said it would avoid English centers.

Spring 1908: HOL-KIE as agreed with France; expect French MUN and possibly English DEN support against Russia. France says it will defend BEL and leave HOL alone; Austria attacks RUM with SER/SEV support.
Press RUM with BUL supported by SER and SEV; AEG advances on SMY, TYR to BOH. Italy promised to keep TRI/VEN clear; France will hold MUN, England contest SWE. Russia remains the solo threat.

Keep TRI defended against Russia; A VEN supports F TRI holding. Austria and I agreed to avoid opening a front; Russia says it targets Austria, not Italy. Stage westward via MAO/GOL while retaining POR and coordinating against Russia.

BEL to HOL as Germany vacates; MUN supports Germany’s HOL–KIE, BUR supports MUN holding against BER. ENG to PIC and YOR to WAL, staying out of English centers as promised. Austria and England coordinate against Russia; reassess German cooperation after this turn.

Press DEN with BAL supported by KIE and SWE; attack BUL with RUM supported by BLA and CON, and SEV with UKR supported by MOS. Keep BUD defended; BER advances to SIL. England and Austria remain openly hostile; Italy refuses cooperation.

messages.body: Your A BUL, A CON, and A SEV threaten my RUM and SMY. Are you attacking either this fall? I will defend my remaining centers and cannot agree to further Russian gains. If you want a quieter frontier, keep A CON out of RUM and SMY.

Please keep F TRI in TRI and A VEN out of Austrian centers this fall, as agreed. Russia is pressing my remaining centers; can you keep the Austrian frontier quiet while you continue to pressure Russia?

Russia remains the solo threat. Please use A HOL and A MUN to pressure BER this fall if feasible, and keep your units clear of Austrian centers. I’m defending my southern frontier against Russian gains.

Are F BAL and F SWE targeting DEN again this fall, and what is A FIN doing? I’ll defend my remaining centers; I won’t trade away DEN or leave your northern centers uncontested. If you keep your fleets clear of NOR and NTH, we can avoid widening the English-Russian front.

Russia still threatens a solo. Which Russian-held centers are you targeting this fall with A RUM, A SER, and F SMY? Please focus on denying Russia RUM, SEV, or SMY rather than opening a front against Italy; I’ll keep defending DEN and contesting Russia in the north.

Please keep A WAL and your other units clear of EDI and my remaining centers this fall. Are you pressing Russia from the east, especially against A KIE or A BER? I’m defending DEN and NOR and need France focused on containing Russia rather than expanding into English centers.

Russia can still grow this fall. What are A BOH, A GRE, A RUM, A SER, and F SMY doing? Please prioritize denying Russia’s gains; I can use A MUN to pressure BER if you’re attacking Russian units nearby.
Russia’s northern centers remain vulnerable. What are F DEN, F NOR, and F NTH targeting this fall? Please contest F SWE or another Russian center, and avoid opening a front against my units.
I’ll leave A KIE alone. Could A KIE support my A MUN–BER this fall? That would put pressure on Russia’s A BER while A HOL stays to secure HOL. What are you planning for KIE?
